purpose: Specify synthetic local-query correctness, cursor, summary, page-budget, coverage, and performance scenarios before T10 implementation.

dependencyGateDetails.rule: Until both dependencies are accepted, only independent synthetic fixture/interface preparation is allowed. Do not implement T10 production behavior, connect a fake-success repository, or run behavior/performance tests.

sections: §5.5 丢钥、卸载与备份恢复 gate

fixturePolicy.fixedSeed: Use a recorded deterministic seed for synthetic entities; the seed creates no data from a user profile.
neverUse: live user profile or installed application database
fixturePolicy.queryContract: Use only the HistoryQuery and ItemSummary fields already described in docs/spec/02-architecture.md §4. Do not add query fields or alter contracts/schema during this fixture preparation.
fixturePolicy.limitsSource: Read page item, serialized page byte, preview character, and performance targets from docs/spec/limits.v1.json. Do not copy threshold values into fixture-local constants.
fixturePolicy.frozenSearchSemantics: Search/index matching uses Unicode NFKC and case-insensitive matching, including Chinese one/two/three-character substrings and tags; result ordering is (capturedAt or updatedAt DESC, id DESC); a cursor carries sort values and a query fingerprint; query changes invalidate the old cursor.
fixturePolicy.unfrozenBehavior: Do not invent fromUtc/toUtc equality inclusivity, malformed-query error codes, behavior for a single otherwise-valid summary that alone exceeds the page-byte cap, or the query response/error/coverage mapping when local vault or query-store access is unavailable. Cases needing these rules remain NOT_RUN until specified.
fixturePolicy.statusMeaning: NOT_RUN means no behavior has been verified. This plan and its synthetic data definitions are preparation only.

fixtureFamilies.input: A fixed synthetic set of text and saved records with Chinese one-, two-, and three-character matches, longer substring matches, tags, and full-width/case variants. Include a synthetic body whose original bytes differ from its NFKC-normalized search form.
fixtureFamilies.action: Query using each short Chinese term, a substring, a Unicode compatibility variant, and a case variant where applicable; then read/copy the matched synthetic source through the fixture interface without editing it.
fixtureFamilies.expected: Search matches follow NFKC, case-insensitive, substring semantics for Chinese one/two/three-character terms and tags, including matches beyond whole-token FTS behavior. Search/index normalization does not rewrite the original body; reading/copying returns the original synthetic bytes/content. Query summaries contain only summary fields, not the source body.
fixtureFamilies.observation: Compare returned synthetic IDs to the deterministic expected set for each query; capture the original source bytes before/after; inspect returned summary fields for body absence.
specLinks: docs/spec/tasks/T10.md · 子任务顺序 a-b / 完成标准

fixtureFamilies.input: Synthetic items vary by kind, tag text, sourceAppId, deviceId, capturedAt/updatedAt, area, and collectionId, with timestamp samples strictly inside or outside the selected range (no equality-boundary sample).
fixtureFamilies.action: Run text/tag search alone and with combinations of the existing HistoryQuery kind, source, device, date, area, and collection fields.
fixtureFamilies.expected: Each combined query returns exactly the intersection of its specified search and filter criteria. The fixture uses only fields in the frozen HistoryQuery interface and does not assume whether fromUtc/toUtc include an item exactly at the endpoint.
fixtureFamilies.observation: Record query field values, deterministic expected ID set, returned ordered IDs, and any cursor; confirm excluded synthetic items do not appear.
specLinks: docs/spec/tasks/T10.md · 子任务顺序 a / 完成标准

fixtureFamilies.input: A static synthetic result set with tied capturedAt values for history or tied updatedAt values for saved items, deterministic distinct IDs, and enough matching records to cross multiple page boundaries.
fixtureFamilies.action: Read all successive pages with the returned opaque cursor under one unchanged query and generation; separately read the full expected result set from the deterministic fixture oracle.
fixtureFamilies.expected: The result order follows the specified timestamp descending, then ID descending tie-break. Concatenated pages equal the fixture oracle exactly, with no duplicates or missing IDs. This externally checks cursor pagination outcomes without requiring inspection of the query implementation or decoding cursor internals.
fixtureFamilies.observation: Record per-page ordered IDs, opaque cursor presence, final concatenated IDs, and set/order comparison against the synthetic oracle.
specLinks: docs/spec/tasks/T10.md · 子任务顺序 a / 完成标准

fixtureFamilies.input: A synthetic result set and first-page cursor produced by query A; query B changes a search or filter field while retaining the old cursor.
fixtureFamilies.action: Submit query B with query A's cursor, then submit a fresh query B request without that cursor.
fixtureFamilies.expected: The old cursor is not silently accepted as a continuation for the changed query fingerprint. The result explicitly reports cursor invalidation or clearly starts a fresh query-B page; it does not mix query-A and query-B results. Exact error-code spelling is left to the canonical error contract.
fixtureFamilies.observation: Compare query-B response generation/IDs to a fresh query-B first page and record whether the old cursor was rejected or restarted; assert no old-query continuation is returned.
specLinks: docs/spec/tasks/T10.md · 子任务顺序 a / 完成标准

fixtureFamilies.input: A synthetic query held at an injectable query-worker barrier, followed by a newer query generation; a second synthetic profile namespace has distinguishable result IDs.
fixtureFamilies.action: Hold query A, start query B with a newer generation, then switch the active synthetic profile before releasing query A. Release responses in reverse order.
fixtureFamilies.expected: The old generation is canceled or discarded and cannot publish a success page after query B/profile switch. Returned pages are bound to the active request generation and synthetic profile; no result from the prior profile is exposed through the new query/event state.
fixtureFamilies.observation: Record request IDs/generations, active profile namespace, response completion order, emitted page IDs/generation, and stale-result suppression.

fixtureFamilies.input: A synthetic local profile with known indexed item IDs and protected synthetic content; an injected query-store/vault adapter reports temporarily unavailable or access denied before reading it.
fixtureFamilies.action: Issue a synthetic HistoryQuery under each injected access outcome, observe the returned query/page/coverage state without requiring a particular response shape, then restore fake access and issue a fresh query.
fixtureFamilies.expected: OPEN QUESTION: the specification does not freeze the exact query response, error, or coverage mapping for unavailable/denied local access. Do not invent an error code or report protected rows as a verified empty, complete result. Preserve the synthetic profile; while access is unavailable, return no protected content.
fixtureFamilies.observation: Record only the adapter access outcome, whether a page/result/error was emitted and its non-content status fields, and before/after synthetic profile identity and ID set. Do not store protected synthetic content in evidence.
fixtureFamilies.gate: OPEN_QUESTION: query result/error/coverage presentation for local-vault or query-store access failure is not frozen.
specLinks: docs/spec/tasks/T10.md · 完成标准与行为测试

fixtureFamilies.input: Synthetic text and image records with source bodies/attachments longer or larger than summary fields, including a preview at and beyond limits.content.maxPreviewCharacters and a page whose next whole summary would exceed the current page's remaining limits.transport.summaryPageBytes even though each individual complete summary is smaller than the full page-byte cap.
fixtureFamilies.action: Query the records and measure the serialized QueryPage response; advance to the next page using the returned cursor.
fixtureFamilies.expected: Every preview is at or below maxPreviewCharacters. ItemSummary/QueryPage does not contain body text, DataURL, original image bytes, or keys. The complete serialized response stays within summaryPageBytes; if the next complete item would exceed the remaining page budget, the page ends before that item and returns a cursor so no item is truncated or skipped.
fixtureFamilies.observation: Record serialized response byte length, item count, preview character count, field names present, forbidden field/content scan result without storing matched content, and next-page IDs.

fixtureFamilies.input: A synthetic query result set with at least one more matching item than limits.transport.summaryPageItems; every individual summary is otherwise known to fit the page-byte limit.
fixtureFamilies.action: Request a page at the supported maximum and traverse cursors through the whole static result set.
fixtureFamilies.expected: No page contains more than the canonical summaryPageItems limit; the next cursor continues from the first unreturned item. Concatenated pages contain each expected result once. The case avoids a single summary larger than the whole page-byte cap because that behavior is not specified.
fixtureFamilies.observation: Record each page item count, next cursor, and concatenated IDs versus the deterministic fixture oracle.

fixtureFamilies.input: A deterministic synthetic dataset built from a fixed seed with 10,000 text items; place a unique search match after the first unfiltered page in the frozen sort order, and provide a fixture index mode that can expose either the full set or a known incomplete subset.
fixtureFamilies.action: Search for the unique term and query through the result cursor. Run once with the full synthetic set indexed and once with indexing deliberately paused at a known subset.
fixtureFamilies.expected: The unique match is found even though its source item sorts beyond the first unfiltered page; search is not limited to scanning/rendering only that first page. Full-index coverage reports the known indexed entity count and complete state; partial-index coverage reports the known subset and incomplete state rather than implying the entire dataset was searched.
fixtureFamilies.observation: Compare returned IDs and coverage fields against fixed-seed fixture metadata, including indexedEntities and complete; record the synthetic index frontier without using profile data.
specLinks: docs/spec/tasks/T10.md · 子任务顺序 c / 完成标准

fixtureFamilies.input: The fixed-seed 10,000-item synthetic text dataset with documented machine, OS, build, cache, and query conditions.
fixtureFamilies.action: After dependencies and implementation are accepted, measure normal first-page searches under the fixed environment and preserve correctness assertions for Chinese short terms, substrings, combined filters, and beyond-first-page hits.
fixtureFamilies.expected: Compare the measured first-page P95 to limits.performanceTargets.search10000ItemsFirstPageP95Ms using the sample-count and reporting rules in acceptance-matrix §4. A performance miss does not permit weakening search semantics. No measurement or target pass is claimed by this plan.
fixtureFamilies.observation: Eventually record seed, machine/OS, build, cache/network conditions, sample count, p50/p95/max/failure count, query classes, and correctness results; never use real profile data.
specLinks: docs/spec/tasks/T10.md · 完成标准与行为测试

requiredNotRunGates.reason: T10 depends on T07 and T09. Search implementation and behavior tests remain gated until both are accepted.
T06 canonical strict schemas/DTO generation remain in progress. Do not edit contracts/schema, generated output, or invent exact malformed-query/cursor error codes in this fixture preparation.

The specs require preserving data and restricting protected content while vault/access is unavailable, but do not freeze the exact HistoryQuery result, error, or coverage mapping. The synthetic fixture stays gated and asserts no status/error code.

The referenced query interface provides fromUtc/toUtc but does not state endpoint inclusivity. Current fixtures use timestamps strictly inside/outside the range; equality-edge assertions wait for a frozen rule.

The specs require bounded pages without truncating an item but do not define the response when one otherwise-valid summary alone exceeds the entire page-byte cap. The planned byte-boundary case avoids that input.
No T10 search behavior or performance run has been performed. Future acceptance requires the fixed environment and sample/reporting rules in 08 §4.

acceptanceReminder: All cases are synthetic and NOT_RUN. This plan does not implement search, finalize pending DTO schemas, inspect any profile data, or establish performance. Keep T10 status not_started until T07/T09 dependencies, behavior tests, evidence, and required review are complete.
